sections.heading: How Lunar Months Differ from Solar Months
paragraphs: A Hijri month is either 29 or 30 days long, determined by the visibility of the new crescent moon. A Gregorian month is fixed at 28 to 31 days by civil agreement regardless of astronomical events. This fundamental difference means the two calendars drift apart by about eleven days each year.

Over a 33-year cycle the drift completes a full cycle, which is why some communities use a tabular approach that averages the drift for long-range planning. Other communities rely on actual moon sighting, producing slight regional variations in date boundaries.

The converter supports recognized mathematical approximations that match the most common civil and religious expectations, while acknowledging that local moon-sighting authorities may announce dates one day differently.
